title: EXP-024-R2 — Clean Replay: Additional Designer Launch From Live Unobstructed Web Client
objective: Independently replay EXP-024 with the inherited browser state left intact. First enumerate every page/window known to the controlled Playwright browser context and require the clean replay baseline of exactly one retained Web Client and one retained original Web Designer, with no unexpected modal or authentication challenge. If that baseline is not already present, capture the mismatch and stop without normalizing it. If it is present, open one fresh Select Form dialog only as a Web Client functional/liveness indication, capture its populated or error state, and cancel it normally without opening a Form. Then verify that the Select Form dialog is gone, the semantic "Open designer in a new window" command is visibly present/enabled, and the previously observed EXP-023 obstruction has not visibly recurred. Perform exactly one native activation of that command. Record the activation/tool result separately from the browser postcondition, immediately enumerate the controlled Playwright pages/windows, and determine whether a distinct additional Designer page/window is rendered regardless of any Playwright timeout/error. If a newly rendered Designer presents the normal editing-scope dialog, selecting User and confirming is permitted solely to establish rendered new-client UI. Do not infer backend-session identity, transient focus history, popup mechanism, cache/database behavior, or causes not directly evidenced.

Read-only initial enumeration of every page/window known to the controlled Playwright browser context
Read-only capture of the retained Web Client and retained original Designer baseline, including visible dialogs, selected Designer Form/tab, dirty indicators, and displayed editing scope

Close that Select Form dialog through ordinary Cancel without selecting or opening a Form

Capture the post-Cancel rendered/accessibility state showing the dialog gone, the semantic "Open designer in a new window" command visibly present/enabled, and whether the previously observed pointer-interception/visible obstruction has recurred
Perform exactly one native activation of "Open designer in a new window"
Record activation/tool status independently from the post-activation page/window enumeration
Immediately enumerate every page/window known to the controlled Playwright browser context after the single activation
If and only if a distinct newly rendered Designer page/window appears and presents the normal editing-scope dialog, select User and confirm solely to establish rendered new-Designer UI
Write only the EXP-024-R2 experiment record and evidence/EXP-024-R2/
out_of_scope: Any Form, component, variable, Caption, Description, event, script, layout, preference, database, or persistence mutation

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security

If initial enumeration is anything other than exactly one retained Web Client plus one retained original Designer in the expected clean replay state, capture the mismatch and stop; do not close, open, navigate, reload, replace, or otherwise normalize browser state
If an unexpected modal or rendered authentication/session-establishment challenge is present at initial preflight or appears before the launch step, capture it and stop without attempting recovery

Do not create, open for editing, save, regenerate, close, modify, or delete any Form or component; Select Form may be opened only for the functional/liveness check and must be cancelled without opening a Form
Do not invoke Unload All Global Form Objects or mutate User Preferences

Do not describe the launch command as pointer-actionable before the single native activation; before activation report only visible presence/enabled state and whether the known obstruction recurred
Do not activate the Designer launch command more than once, even if Playwright reports timeout/error, no new page is immediately visible, or the result is ambiguous

Do not infer absence of every hidden overlay from screenshots or accessibility state; report only whether the previously observed visible/pointer interception recurred

acceptance_checks.description: Initial read-only enumeration shows exactly one retained Web Client and exactly one retained original Web Designer in the controlled Playwright browser context, with no unexpected extra page/window, missing client, modal obstruction, or rendered authentication/session-establishment challenge. Evidence captures the Designer's selected Form/tab, visible dirty indicators/dialog state, and displayed editing scope. If this exact baseline is not already present, the experiment stops as blocked without any browser-state normalization.

A fresh Select Form dialog is opened read-only and its visible populated/error state is captured as a Web Client functional/liveness indication; no Form is opened. A fresh successful server-backed round trip may be claimed only if ordinary trace/network evidence from that same dialog opening independently shows the corresponding successful request. Otherwise the evidence is explicitly limited to the observed functional/UI indication.

Select Form is closed through ordinary Cancel. Post-close screenshot plus accessibility evidence show the dialog visibly gone, the semantic "Open designer in a new window" command visibly present/enabled, and whether the previously observed EXP-023 interception/visible obstruction recurs. AC-3 makes no claim that the control is pointer-actionable; that is learned only from AC-4.

Exactly one native activation of the semantic "Open designer in a new window" command is attempted. Evidence records the activation/tool status independently as completed/dispatched, timeout/interception, or other explicit tool/browser error. No second activation or alternate launch route occurs.

Immediately after the single activation, every page/window known to the controlled Playwright browser context is enumerated independently of AC-4's tool status. The browser postcondition is recorded as either: (a) a distinct additional Designer page/window is enumerated, or (b) no distinct additional Designer page/window is enumerated. If (a), URL/title/rendered UI establish that page as Designer; any normal scope dialog may be completed as User solely to establish rendered new-client UI. A Playwright timeout/error does not negate (a) if the additional Designer is independently enumerated. If (b), record narrow reproduction of EXP-024's non-production of the documented new-tab/window UI result under the tested retained-Designer condition, without generalizing that multiple Designers are unsupported.

A final read-only capture records the rendered/accessibility state of the retained Web Client, retained original Designer, and any newly enumerated Designer after classification. The worker summary explicitly separates activation/tool status from browser postcondition and states that final-state evidence does not establish transient focus history, unenumerated OS/browser processes, popup mechanism, backend/session validity, hidden cache state, or database state.

Repository/evidence audit confirms no Mongoose artifact was created or modified and writes are confined to experiments/EXP-024-R2-*.md plus evidence/EXP-024-R2/. The final classification states only whether EXP-024's browser-level result reproduced; no reusable launch recipe is promoted unless a distinct additional Designer was actually rendered and all required observable postconditions were satisfied.

initial_instruction: Begin with read-only preflight only. Read EXP-024, EXP-023, and EXP-009-R2, then enumerate every page/window known to the controlled Playwright browser context. Proceed only if the inherited state already contains exactly one retained Web Client and one retained original Designer with no unexpected modal or session challenge; otherwise capture the mismatch and stop without changing browser state. If the baseline passes, open one fresh Select Form dialog as a functional/liveness indication, capture its populated or error state and any ordinary trace evidence already produced by that same opening, then cancel the dialog normally. Capture the post-Cancel launch surface and stop before activating "Open designer in a new window". Report AC-1 through AC-3 only.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261006-153736-D83j. Rationale: EXP-024 supplied one accepted browser-level observation: after the inherited Select Form dialog was cancelled, the previously observed EXP-023 pointer interception did not recur and one native "Open designer in a new window" activation dispatched, yet no distinct additional Designer page/window was enumerated in the controlled Playwright browser context. Current Mongoose documentation describes the expected command result as Web Designer opening in a new browser tab/window, so the smallest useful next step is an independent clean replay of that exact retained-Designer condition. This revision keeps the evidence claims narrow: a populated Select Form is only a functional/liveness indication unless trace evidence from that same opening proves a fresh successful request; pre-launch evidence establishes only that the launch command is visibly present/enabled and the known obstruction has not recurred, while actual pointer-actionability is learned from the single activation; activation/tool status and browser postcondition are recorded independently; and the run stops immediately if the inherited browser baseline is not already the required retained Web Client plus retained original Designer state. No browser-state normalization, blocked-experiment workaround, artifact mutation, second launch, or hidden-mechanism diagnosis is permitted.
